facts.text: Sojourner Rover was deployed at Ares Vallis during Mars Pathfinder in 1997.

Sojourner was the first rover to operate on another planet. Weighing just 10.6 kg (about the size of a microwave oven), it explored about 100 square metres of the surface over 83 sols. Sojourner carried an Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer to analyse rock compositions, finding that some rocks were similar to Earth's andesite.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Performed the first rover-based chemical analysis of Martian rocks, revealing unexpectedly silicon-rich compositions similar to Earth's andesite.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Ares Vallis.
Sojourner last communicated on 27 September 1997; it likely sits within a few metres of the base station, its solar panels long covered in dust.
